opex.text: Liquidity management is required to ensure that adequate funds will be available to meet anticipated and unanticipated deposit withdrawals, debt service payments, investment commitments, commercial and consumer loan demand, and ongoing operating expenses. Funding sources include principal repayments on loans, sale of assets, growth in time and core deposits, short and long-term borrowings, investment securities coming due, loan prepayments and repurchase agreements. Regular loan payments are a dependable source of funds, while the sale of investment securities, deposit growth and loan prepayments are significantly influenced by general economic conditions and the level of interest rates.

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
A summary of the provision for credit losses for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, is as follows:

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, there was a provision for credit losses of $942,000, an increase of $463,000 in expense compared to a provision for credit losses of $479,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The provision for the three months ended September 30, 2026 included expense related to loans receivable of $821,000 and off-balance sheet exposures of $121,000. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, there was a provision for credit losses of $1,405,000, an increase of $562,000 in expense compared to a provision for credit losses of $843,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonint.text:
Total non-interest expense increased $70,000 or 0.7% from $9,978,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, to $10,048,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026. Salaries and employee benefits expense of $5,417,000 for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $618,000 from $4,799,000 for same period in 2025. This increase was related to health insurance expenses associated with the Corporation’s partially self-funded health insurance plan which were $422,000 higher for the three months ended September 30, 2026 than the same period in 2025, along with ongoing salary and wage increases for employees. The increase in salaries and employee benefits expense was partially offset by a decrease in professional fees of $164,000 due primarily to lower legal and consulting costs and a decrease in other non-interest expense of $351,000 due primarily to lower overall marketing and advertising costs comparing the three months ended September 30, 2026 to the same period in 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, total non-interest expense decreased $260,000 or 0.8% to $30,665,000, compared to $30,925,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. Salaries and employee benefits expense of $16,330,000 for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased $227,000 from $16,103,000 for the same period of 2025.

net.text: Financial Accounting Standards Board (“FASB”) Accounting Standards Codification (“ASC”) 326, Financial Instruments – Credit Losses , provides guidance on the accounting for credit losses for most financial assets and certain other instruments that are not measured at fair value through net income. ASC 326 requires consideration of a broad range of reasonable and supportable information to form credit loss estimates in an effort to provide financial statement users with more decision-useful information about the expected credit losses on financial instruments and other commitments to extend credit. Commonly referred to as Current Expected Credit Losses (“CECL”), ASC 326 requires a financial asset (or a group of financial assets) to be measured at an amortized cost basis and presented at the net amount expected to be collected. ASC 326 affects financial assets and net investment in leases that are not accounted for at fair value through net income, including such financial assets as loans, debt securities, trade receivables, net investments in leases, off-balance sheet credit exposures, reinsurance receivables, and any other financial assets not excluded from the scope that have the contractual right to receive cash.

da.text: Net cash outflows from investing activities used $47.0 million of cash and cash equivalents during the nine months ended September 30, 2026. Accounting for the majority of the net cash outflows was $76.4 million related to proceeds from sales, paydowns, calls and maturities of available-for-sale debt securities which was offset by purchases of available-for-sale debt securities of $90.8 million and a net increase in loans of $35.4 million, which reflected strong loan demand. Financing activities provided $4.7 million in net cash, which resulted primarily from a $59.0 million increase in deposits, partially offset by $41.0 million repayment of long-term borrowings, a net decrease in short-term borrowings of $4.9 million along with cash dividends paid of $8.5 million. Operating activities include net income, adjusted for the effects of non-cash transactions including, among others, depreciation and amortization and the provision for credit losses, and is the primary source of cash flows from operations. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating activities provided the Corporation with $29.5 million in net cash, which primarily reflected net income of $20.4 million and proceeds from the sale of mortgage loans of $23.8 million.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income is the difference between (i) interest income, interest and fees on interest-earning assets, and (ii) interest expense, interest paid on deposits and borrowed funds. Net interest income represents the largest component of the Corporation’s operating income and, as such, is the primary determinant of profitability. Net interest income is impacted by variations in the volume, rate and composition of earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, changes in general market interest rates and the level of non-performing assets. Interest income is shown on a fully tax-equivalent basis using the corporate statutory tax rate of 21.0% in 2026 and 2025.

Tax-equivalent net interest income increased $2.0 million, or 12.4%, to $17.9 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $15.9 million for the same period in 2025. The increase in tax-equivalent net interest income was due to an increase in tax-equivalent interest income reflecting higher earning asset volumes and yields, along with a decrease in interest expense which resulted primarily from a significant decrease in average borrowings coupled with a decrease in the average rate paid on total interest-bearing liabilities.
